'''Peter Hausen''' (2 January 1935 – 28 May 2012) was a German [[developmental biologist]] who spent most of his career at the [[Max Planck Institute for Developmental Biology]], where he was appointed Director of the Department of Cell Biology in 1973. Hausen died in 2012.<ref name="mpi">{{cite web|last1=Biology|first1=Max Planck Institute for Developmental|title=History|url=http://www.eb.tuebingen.mpg.de/institute/history.html|website=www.eb.tuebingen.mpg.de|accessdate=24 March 2017|language=en}}</ref><ref name="obit">{{cite journal|last1=Winklbauer|first1=Rudi|title=Obituary - In Memoriam: Prof. Peter Hausen|journal=Mechanisms of Development|date=July 2012|volume=129|issue=5–8|pages=192|doi=10.1016/j.mod.2012.06.003|doi-access=}}</ref>

==Education and academic career==
Hausen received his Ph.D. in 1961, supervised by [[Werner Scäfer]] at what was then the Max Planck Institute for Virology. After a brief stay as a visiting scientist at the [[Weizmann Institute]] in Israel, he returned to Germany to join the [[Max Planck Institute for Biology]]. He then moved back to MPI for Virology (which later changed its name and research focus to [[Max Planck Institute for Developmental Biology]]) and became the Director of the Department of Cell Biology in 1973. He was also active in the establishment of the [[Max Planck Institute for Chemical Ecology]].<ref name=obit />

==Research==
Hausen's research focused on [[developmental biology]].<ref name=obit /> In the course of his work on [[cellular differentiation]] and the [[gene regulation|regulation]] of [[transcription (genetics)|transcription]] in [[eukaryote]]s, his research group discovered [[ribonuclease H]], a family of [[enzyme]]s that selectively degrades the [[RNA]] component of mixed [[RNA]]/[[DNA]] [[double helix|duplexes]].<ref name="stein">{{cite journal|last1=Stein|first1=H.|last2=Hausen|first2=P.|title=Enzyme from Calf Thymus Degrading the RNA Moiety of DNA-RNA Hybrids: Effect on DNA-Dependent RNA Polymerase|journal=Science|date=17 October 1969|volume=166|issue=3903|pages=393–395|doi=10.1126/science.166.3903.393|pmid=5812039}}</ref><ref name="hausen">{{cite journal|last1=Hausen|first1=Peter|last2=Stein|first2=Hans|title=Ribonuclease H. An Enzyme Degrading the RNA Moiety of DNA-RNA Hybrids|journal=European Journal of Biochemistry|date=June 1970|volume=14|issue=2|pages=278–283|doi=10.1111/j.1432-1033.1970.tb00287.x|pmid=5506170|doi-access=free}}</ref> He is especially well recognized for studies of the development of the [[model organism]] ''[[Xenopus laevis]]'' (African clawed frog). With [[Metta Riebesell]], he coauthored a widely used and well-reviewed reference work on the topic, ''The early development of Xenopus laevis. An atlas of the histology.''<ref name="yost">{{cite journal|last1=Yost|first1=H.Joseph|title=The early development of Xenopus laevis: An Atlas of the histology|journal=Trends in Genetics|date=May 1992|volume=8|issue=5|pages=186|doi=10.1016/0168-9525(92)90222-P}}</ref>
